newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Neves Corvo copper unions, management in deal.
newsitem.headline: Neves Corvo copper unions, management in deal.

text.p: Representatives of miners and management at the Neves Corvo copper mine in southern Portugal reached agreement on Monday on the working of Sunday shifts, a company spokesman told Reuters.
The spokesman said that Somincor, the state-owned company which operates the 107,000 tonnes per year mine, had sealed the deal in talks with miners leaders on Monday.
"Somincor reached an agreement on operating the mine seven days a week, 24 hours a day," the spokesman said.
Miners leaders were not immediately available for comment. Any accord would need to be voted on by an assembly of miners at the site, 250 km south of Lisbon.
The issue of Sunday working, which management says is necessary to boost efficiency, triggered a five-day strike at Neves Corvo earlier this month.
Last Thursday miners voted to reject an earlier management proposal involving an increased number of free days in return for working Sundays
